Anika — thanks for the clear asks and the template. We'll prepare a concise response and include the requested artifacts. High-level answers now so you have context before the full packet: 

- RTO: our standard target for hosted API endpoints is <= 90s for single-request tail latency recovery (transparent fallback to a compatible model variant) and 15m for full control-plane-driven recovery to restore service routing after major region loss.
- RPO: we maintain stateless request processing for transient inference calls; for customer-managed persistent sessions (Private deployments) RPO is configurable — typical default is < 5 minutes for in-flight session metadata via durable KV replication.
- Failover: automatic request routing to warm standby regions for Hosted customers using health-check-driven routing and cross-region replication of essential metadata; automatic failover is enabled for accounts on enterprise plans by default. Manual runbook-driven failover is available for Dedicated/Private where customers prefer control.
- Exercises: runbooks are exercised quarterly for control plane scenarios and annually for full-region evacuation drills; last partial exercise (control-plane failover sim) completed 2026-09-14.

We'll attach a redacted runbook extract and the recent exercise summary in our packet. Would you like the answers inline in the XLSX or as a consolidated PDF?

—Karthik

Anika — attaching the packet as discussed. I put our short answers inline in the spreadsheet and included two artifacts: a redacted runbook extract and the exercise summary. Highlights: 

- Typical recovery timeline: control-plane routing switch (auto) ~30–120s depending on DNS propagation and client-side retry window; full orchestration rollback for large-scale migrations ~10–20 minutes to re-establish capacity and routable endpoints depending on model size.
- Cross-region replication: metadata is replicated using encrypted streaming replication to at least one warm standby region; token caches are not replicated across regions but we rehydrate on-demand.
- Monitoring: we publish health metrics and alert hooks via our Console (alerts for instance termination, queue depth, tail-latency spikes). We also provide a webhook for incident-forwarding and integrations with PagerDuty/SFN.

Quick technical note for Anika / Tom: 

- RTO/RPO by model family (typical production config, enterprise plan):
  * 7B-family: RTO (service routing recover) ~30–60s; RPO ~0 (stateless inference)
  * 13B-family: RTO ~45–90s; RPO ~0
  * 70B-family: RTO ~60–120s; RPO ~0

- Warm standby design: instances in standby region keep warmed weights and a small pre-allocated KV cache to reduce cold-starts for the most common prefixes. When failover triggers, we route traffic to standby and the runtime fills larger KV entries async; this is why initial requests may see slightly higher median latency but tail recovery is within the RTO window.

- For Private deployments: customers can elect synchronous KV replication across two sites (RPO < 1s) but that requires network and storage topology adjustments — we document tradeoffs in Appendix B of the runbook.

If you want, we can run a tabletop with your infra team and simulate a region failover next month.

—Jonas
